trials.notes: Used the documented Tag Processor template-building pattern directly: predeclared attributes preserve order, placeholder text creates a replaceable #text token, set_attribute()/set_modifiable_text() receive plain strings, and get_updated_html() returns the edited fragment. Passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

Equivalent to the canonical documented approach. All called APIs are present in the rendered docs: constructor, next_tag(), set_attribute(), next_token(), get_token_type(), set_modifiable_text(), and get_updated_html(). Passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

All API calls are documented, including WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and inherited Tag Processor mutation/output methods. The result is correct, but the processor choice is less idiomatic: the task is flat template filling, which the docs route to WP_HTML_Tag_Processor, not the heavier tree-aware HTML Processor. The unbounded token walk after FIGCAPTION is acceptable only because the template is fixed. Passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: No hidden cases failed in this round. The docs did well on the exact risks this task probes: the Tag Processor “Building markup from a template” section explicitly says to seed attributes in the desired order and include placeholder text; set_attribute() documents that plain unescaped values are encoded and that newly added attributes sort by name; set_modifiable_text() documents that it operates on #text/modifiable tokens, cannot insert into an empty element, and encodes plaintext; get_updated_html() is documented as the correct way to retrieve queued mutations. The main near-miss is trial-3’s processor choice: the HTML Processor docs do explain that structure-aware parsing is for containment/subtree work, while flat exact-preservation edits fit the Tag Processor, but the HTML Processor overview still makes it plausible to choose create_fragment() for any fragment construction task. That choice did not break these cases because get_updated_html() was used rather than serialize().

doc_gaps.problem: The page says the HTML Processor safely parses and modifies fragments, but its early examples can make it look like the default choice for any fragment work, including literal-template construction where tree awareness is unnecessary.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short “Prefer WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for known-template filling and byte-exact output” note near Usage, cross-linking to the Tag Processor template-building section and warning that HTML Processor is for tree-aware queries/normalization/unsupported-markup policy.

doc_gaps.problem: A user can call inherited Tag Processor methods such as set_modifiable_text() and get_updated_html(), but the HTML Processor method index does not make the inherited template-editing surface easy to discover as a group.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an “Inherited editing APIs” subsection listing set_attribute(), set_modifiable_text(), and get_updated_html(), with one sentence that queued mutations should be read with get_updated_html(), not serialize().

doc_gaps.problem: The docs cover encoding and boolean values, but the string/boolean/null edge semantics are spread out and easy to miss under task pressure.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact value-semantics table: string including '' writes a quoted value, true writes a boolean attribute, false removes the attribute, and null is not an accepted setter value.

doc_gaps.problem: The placeholder-text requirement is documented well, but examples with multiple possible text nodes could still lead users to replace the first later #text token outside their intended element.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note that after locating a container element, callers should constrain the token walk by known template shape, depth, breadcrumbs, or a specific target tag when more than one text node may follow.
